pull.title: feat(reasoning): give a thinking turn the model's whole output allowance, and ship the ceiling set
pull.body:
# Reasoning gets the model's whole output allowance, and the ceiling becomes your head

A thinking request is now sized from what the routed model can actually emit, not from a number the client picked for an answer. `MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS_CEILING` ships set at **131,072** as the head on that. A model that publishes no reasoning control keeps the rung it was asked for. `thinking_chars` records a measured **0** instead of NULL. And the request-detail wire pane now names every parameter the body carried, widening included.

## What was wrong

**Reasoning could only ever narrow `max_tokens`, never widen it.** All four steps in `resolve_max_output_tokens` clamp down, and the number they clamp is `routed.request.max_tokens` — the client's own ask. Nothing in the chain knew the request was a thinking request. Thinking tokens and answer tokens come out of that one allowance (WORKING-NOTES §54), so a client that sized `max_tokens` for an answer had unknowingly sized the thinking too.

Measured: on Command Code at effort `max` with `max_tokens 8000`, the host produced **9,024 tokens of thinking and a one-character answer**. The rung was right; the allowance it was spent from was the client's, and the client had no way to know the route was a thinking route.

On a 262,144-output model with a 64,000 ask at `max`:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| wire `max_tokens` | 64,000 | 131,072 |
| answer reserve `min(16384, output // 2)` | 16,384 | 16,384 |
| thinking budget at ratio 0.95 | `min(60,800, 47,616)` = **47,616** | `min(124,518, 114,688)` = **114,688** |
| answer room left | 16,384 | 16,384 |

**`_drop_controls` read the wrong boolean.** A model publishing `reasoning_options: []` — about 23% of models.dev's reasoning catalogue — reached `_drop_controls`, which decided on `dialect.toggle` raw. On Command Code, whose only on-channel is `reasoning_effort` with `enabled_value="max"`, an explicit `low` came back as a bare ON and the encoder spelled it as the host's own `max`. That is byte-for-byte the regression PR G removed for toggle-only models; `_drop_controls` never got the memo — it read `_Channels.default_rung` where it needed `_Channels.on_signal_is_the_effort_field`.

**`thinking_chars` was `self._thinking_chars or None`**, folding "this stream returned no reasoning" into "nobody was counting" — precisely the distinction `reasoning_by_model` exists to report.

**And when the allowance did move, nothing said so.**

## What to expect now

A 64,000-token ask, wire `max_tokens`, at the shipped 131,072 ceiling:

| model output limit | `max` | `high` | `low` | reasoning off |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 16,384 | 16,384 | 16,384 | 16,384 | 16,384 |
| 64,000 | 64,000 | 64,000 | 64,000 | 64,000 |
| 131,072 | 131,072 | 131,072 | 131,072 | 64,000 |
| 262,144 | 131,072 | 131,072 | 131,072 | 64,000 |

The rung does not change the allowance — the *presence* of reasoning does. The rung then decides how much of that allowance the thinking may take, on hosts that speak a numeric budget; on effort-only hosts the rung is untouched and only the answer stops starving. Reasoning off is byte-identical to 6.7.0 except for the new ceiling. A model publishing **less** than the ask is still clamped down to its own limit, as before. An **unknown** limit is never widened — a number nobody published has no standing to raise an explicit request, the same rule that stops it lowering one. `max_tokens: 0` stays 0.

### Live rows

Run through an isolated MCC server on port 8199 with `USERPROFILE` and `HOME` redirected to a scratch home, so `~/.fcc` was never read or written. Client ask `max_tokens: 64000`, `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: 4096}` in (a) and (b).

**(a) `commandcode/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3`, tier `max`** — SSE blocks `thinking` / `thinking_delta` / `text` / `text_delta`:

```
"wire": {"model": "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3", "max_tokens": 131072,
         "reasoning": {"reasoning_effort": "max"}, "stream": true,
         "stream_options": {"include_usage": true}},
"output_widened_from": 64000
thinking_chars 63634   reasoning "control=on,effort=max"
```

**(b) `nvidia_nim/moonshotai/kimi-k3`, tier `max`** — same SSE block kinds:

```
"wire": {"model": "moonshotai/kimi-k3", "max_tokens": 131072,
         "reasoning": {"extra_body.chat_template_kwargs":
                       {"thinking": true, "enable_thinking": true}},
         "stream": true, "stream_options": {"include_usage": true}},
"output_widened_from": 64000
thinking_chars 5490   reasoning "control=on"
```

**(c) the same shape with `thinking: {type: "disabled"}`** on a route whose reasoning preference is `client`:

```
"wire": {"model": "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3", "max_tokens": 64000,
         "stream": true, "stream_options": {"include_usage": true}}
(no output_widened_from)
thinking_chars 0   reasoning "control=off"
```

Rule 1 proven rather than asserted: the client's ask leaves untouched, no widening row, and the completed non-reasoning stream stores a measured `0` rather than a blank — the `thinking_chars` fix, end to end.

**One honest gap in (b).** With the models.dev catalogue present, this deployment of `kimi-k3` resolves as publishing no reasoning control, so gating correctly discards the rung *and* the client's `budget_tokens` (rule 11/12, unchanged by this PR) and the wire carries the chat-template toggle without a `reasoning_budget`. The widening is proven on that route (`64,000 → 131,072`); the *budget sized from the widened allowance* is proven by unit test (`test_the_rung_ratio_applies_to_the_widened_allowance`: 64,000 ask, 262,144 model, 131,072 ceiling → budget 114,688, floor 16,384) rather than by a live row. Stated rather than glossed. For contrast, the same route before the catalogue was seeded — capability unknown, so no widening — sent `max_tokens 64000` with `reasoning_budget: 47616`, which is exactly the starvation this PR removes.

### Browser check

The request-detail modal on the 8199 server, driven in Chrome, no console errors:

- `max_tokens 131,072 · raised from 64,000 for reasoning · reasoning_effort max` on the facts line;
- an `output_widened_from 64000` row in the knobs block;
- the unwidened row shows `max_tokens 64,000` and no widening row at all — absence is the finding;
- the Limits page shows `MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS_CEILING` at `131072`.

Screenshots: `i-after-widened-modal.png`, `i-after-wire-params.png`, `i-after-not-widened.png`, `i-after-ceiling-default.png`.

## Also in this PR: the wire pane names every parameter

`wire_params_summary` kept a hand-picked subset, so the pane could only ever show a knob somebody had thought to list — `stream`, `stream_options`, `tool_choice`, `parallel_tool_calls`, `response_format`, `min_p` and a provider's own `extra_body` entries were invisible. Every non-content key is kept now: the named ones first in their existing order, then every remaining top-level key alphabetically, then every non-reasoning `extra_body` key as `extra_body.<name>`. Content fields stay out — they are content, not parameters, and they are what the body pane degrades when its size cap bites. **The parameter section is never truncated**, because a knob lost to a cap is not recoverable from anywhere else. Redaction is unchanged, and the new tail is redacted as a mapping so a top-level `authorization` is caught by name rather than only by value shape. `buildWireKnobs` renders all of it, above the body, so the pane reads knobs first and structure second.

## Action required

**The ceiling now defaults to 131,072.** Set `MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS_CEILING=0` for no ceiling at all, or your own number.

It ships set because the widening asks for the model's maximum, and OpenAI/Azure-style limiters pre-reserve `max_tokens` against the TPM bucket before generating — so an unbounded thinking turn on a 262,144-output model can 429 a request that would have been served. It applies uniformly, reasoning or not, and it never raises a model above its own published limit.

**Blank no longer means "off".** `blank_limit_falls_back_to_its_default` makes an empty field resolve to the field's default, which is now a number. `0` is the sentinel — the idiom `config/limits.py` already uses for its other three budget keys — and the range widens to `LimitRange(0, 1_048_576)`. The sentinel is re-applied *after* the range clamp too, since that clamp's floor for this key is the sentinel and a literal ceiling of zero would cap every answer at nothing.

## Known and deliberate

- **OpenAI/Azure TPM pre-reservation** is accepted, with the ceiling as the mitigation and the knob.
- **Empty-answer rescue is deferred.** A stream that thinks and then ends cleanly with `finish_reason=length` and an empty visible answer is not rescued. `FALLBACK_ON_REASONING_ONLY` fires from the *deadline* path, and a stream that ended on time, with output, never reaches it — that needs a commit-boundary rule, not a timer. Documented as a known gap in the README, in `docs/USAGE.md` § Deadlines, and on the setting's own card in the admin UI.
- **`output_widened_from` is a per-attempt `params` key, not a `ReasoningAdaptation` kind.** A new kind would touch `core/reasoning.py`, the severity table, `combine_reasoning_adaptations`, the badge lists and four jsdom tests, to describe something that is not a reasoning adaptation at all — the reasoning is exactly what was asked for; only the allowance moved.

## Residual risks

1. **TPM pre-reservation.** A widened reasoning turn can 429 sooner on limiters that reserve `max_tokens` before generating. Mitigated by the 131,072 default; the escape hatch is lowering it.
2. **Longer thinking, more `FALLBACK_REASONING_ANSWER_TIMEOUT`.** A budget host given 114,688 thinking tokens instead of 47,616 can legitimately think past the 300s reasoning-answer deadline, which will now end more attempts. The timer is unchanged; the traffic under it is not.
3. **A behaviour change for operators who wanted no head.** Anyone relying on "the ceiling is unset" gets 131,072 on upgrade, silently, on non-reasoning requests too. Recoverable with `=0`. Blank no longer meaning "off" is the sharpest edge here.
4. **The learned output cap is still per-process.** Widening asks a larger number of an under-reporting provider, so the one 400 that teaches the cap is marginally more reachable on the first reasoning request after a restart. Pre-existing gap.
5. **A no-control model may be handed a rung its own vendor rejects.** The §0.4 fix writes the caller's rung into the host's effort field for a model that publishes no control. A forwarding host that refuses it pays one 400 and is remembered (`openai_chat/reasoning_reject.py`) — the same trade PR G took.
6. **`output_widened_from` is visible only in the wire pane.** Not in the reasoning badge, the severity table, or exports that read only the request row. Deliberate (see above).
7. **Nothing detects a widening that did not help.** A model that spends the whole widened allowance thinking and still answers nothing is the deferred gap above.
8. **The parameter block is now unbounded in key count.** A dialect that sends a very large number of top-level keys makes a longer list. It is bounded by what a real provider body carries, and no key is truncated by design.

## Deviations from the spec, and why

- **`_prepare_from` announces attempt 0 *before* the budgets run**, because preflight has to stay ahead of token counting (WORKING-NOTES §56, pinned by `test_executor_preflight_failure_stays_before_token_count_and_stream`). So `on_attempt` saw the pre-budget object and `output_widened_from` never reached the log. The spec asked this be verified rather than assumed; it is false, and the fix is a **narrow re-announcement** of the prepared attempt after the rebinding, taken only when `output_widened_from` is set. Re-announcing unconditionally doubles the chain's announcement sequence, which is itself a contract that four `test_execution.py` cases assert.
- **`config/settings.py` gained `_no_ceiling_when_zero`**, shared by the field validator and the range clamp. Not in the spec: the clamp's floor for this key *is* the sentinel, so a hand-typed negative resolved to a literal ceiling of 0 and would have capped every answer at nothing. Pinned by `test_a_negative_output_ceiling_lands_on_the_sentinel_not_on_zero`.
- **`tests/config/test_limit_bounds.py::test_a_value_below_the_range_is_clamped_not_fatal`** special-cases the ceiling for the same reason, as the spec anticipated.
- **The browser check ran against 8199's own admin directly** rather than through a static harness on 8099 proxying GETs to 8199. The 8199 server already serves this branch's `admin_static` *and* holds the rows, so the proxy would have added a layer without adding fidelity. Nothing was ever sent to port 8082.

## Baseline

The local suite has **15 pre-existing failures** that fail identically on unmodified `main`: 8 websearch tests that read the real `~/.fcc/.env`, 6 PowerShell installer tests, and `tests/runtime/test_provider_manager.py::test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache`. GitHub runners have no `~/.fcc`, so they pass there.

```
15 failed, 7598 passed, 38 skipped in 113.11s (0:01:53)
```

`ruff format`, `ruff check`, repo-wide `ty check` and the suppression grep are all clean.

commit.message:
feat(reasoning): give a thinking turn the model's whole output allowance

Reasoning could only ever narrow `max_tokens`, never widen it. The four steps
in `resolve_max_output_tokens` all clamp down, and the number they clamp is the
client's own ask -- a number a client sizes for an *answer*, with no idea the
route it landed on is a thinking route. Thinking tokens and answer tokens come
out of that one allowance (WORKING-NOTES 54), so on a 262,144-output model a
64,000 ask left the thinking budget at 47,616 and the answer with 16,384,
whatever the model could actually have done. The live shape of it: Command Code
at effort `max` with `max_tokens 8000` produced 9,024 tokens of thinking and a
one-character answer. The rung was right; the allowance it was spent from was
the client's.

Three smaller defects travelled with it. `_drop_controls` read `dialect.toggle`
raw -- the widest of the three booleans `_Channels` keeps apart -- so a model
publishing `reasoning_options: []` on a host whose only on-signal is its effort
field had an explicit `low` answered with the host's `enabled_value`, `max`.
That is byte-for-byte the regression PR G removed for toggle-only models;
`_drop_controls` never got the memo. `thinking_chars` was stored as
`self._thinking_chars or None`, folding "this stream returned no reasoning" into
"nobody was counting" -- exactly the distinction `reasoning_by_model` exists to
report. And when the allowance did move, nothing said so.

The rule now: when the routed attempt is going to think and the model's output
limit is known, the ask starts at `max(client ask, model limit)`; the model
limit, the unknown fallback, the operator's ceiling and the context headroom
then clamp it in the same order, with the same 4,096 floor, as they clamp any
other ask. Reasoning off is byte-identical to 6.7.0. A no-control model on a
host whose on-signal is the effort field is now handed the caller's own rung,
clamped to the host's enum -- one implementation, `_send_rung_as_on_signal`,
shared with PR G's toggle-only branch so the two cannot drift.

Non-obvious choices. The widening is gated on the reasoning decision, not
applied generally: raising every request's `max_tokens` would be inventing a
limit in the other direction. `MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS_CEILING` therefore ships set at
131,072 -- the operator's head, applied uniformly whether the request reasons or
not -- because OpenAI and Azure style limiters pre-reserve `max_tokens` against
the TPM bucket before generating, so an unbounded thinking turn on a
262,144-output model can 429 a request that would have been served. `0` lifts
it entirely, the idiom `config/limits.py` already uses for its other three
budget keys, and it is needed because `blank_limit_falls_back_to_its_default`
makes a blank field mean the default -- which is now a number. The sentinel is
re-applied after the range clamp too, since that clamp's floor for this key
*is* the sentinel and a literal ceiling of zero would cap every answer at
nothing. An unknown output limit is never widened: a number nobody published has
no standing to raise an explicit request, the same rule that stops it lowering
one. `max_tokens: 0` stays 0. And `output_widened_from` is a per-attempt
`params` key rather than a new `ReasoningAdaptation` kind, because nothing about
the reasoning was adapted -- the reasoning is exactly what was asked for; only
the allowance moved.

The survey this rests on, in one line: OpenRouter and Vercel publish the same
effort-to-budget ratios FCC already uses; 9Router (+1024), OmniRouter (+1000)
and OpenClaw (budget + a 1024 answer floor) all raise `max_tokens` for a
thinking turn, so the idea is not novel -- FCC's version is capability-bounded
rather than a flat constant; no router in the survey learns an allowance from
observed traffic, and this one does not either; and only vLLM and llama.cpp can
force a `</think>`, which is why the answer floor is the only lever that
reserves answer room and widening is the only way to grow it.

Verification. `ruff format`, `ruff check`, repo-wide `ty check` and the
suppression grep are clean. Full `pytest -q`: 15 failed, 7595 passed, 38 skipped
-- exactly the standing baseline (8 websearch tests that read the real
`~/.fcc/.env`, 6 PowerShell installer tests, and
`test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache`), all of which
fail the same way on unmodified `main`. The wire table is the proof for the
gating half: the no-control row on Command Code now reads
`{"reasoning_effort": "low"}`, the same capability on a host with a real toggle
still reads `{"reasoning": {"enabled": true}}`, and on a host with no reasoning
field it still reads `{}`.

Deliberately not done: a stream that thinks and then ends cleanly with an empty
visible answer is still not rescued. `FALLBACK_ON_REASONING_ONLY` fires from the
deadline path, and a stream that ended on time, with output, never reaches it --
that needs a commit-boundary rule rather than a timer. It is documented as a
known gap in the README, in the Deadlines section of `docs/USAGE.md`, and on the
setting's own card in the admin UI.

feat(admin): the wire pane names every parameter the body carried

`wire_params_summary` kept a hand-picked subset -- `model`, `max_tokens` under
its three spellings, a `tools` count, the nine sampling fields and the reasoning
keys -- so the request-detail pane could only ever show a knob somebody had
thought to list. Anything else a dialect sends (`stream`, `stream_options`,
`tool_choice`, `parallel_tool_calls`, `response_format`, `min_p`, a provider's
own `extra_body` entries) was invisible in the parameters block, which is the
first thing anyone opens the pane for.

Every non-content key is kept now: the named ones first, in their existing
deterministic order, then every remaining top-level key alphabetically, then
every non-reasoning `extra_body` key as `extra_body.<name>`. The content fields
stay out -- they are content, not parameters, and they are what the body pane
degrades when its size cap bites; the parameter section is never truncated,
because a knob lost to a cap is not recoverable from anywhere else. Redaction is
unchanged and now runs over the new tail as a mapping, so a top-level
`authorization` is caught by name rather than only by value shape.

`buildWireKnobs` correspondingly renders everything `params.wire` holds instead
of its own hand-picked list, in the same order, above the body itself -- so the
pane reads knobs first and structure second.

Verified in a browser against an isolated server on 8199 (`USERPROFILE` and
`HOME` redirected; `~/.fcc` never touched): a live Command Code attempt renders
`model / max_tokens / output_widened_from / reasoning_effort / stream /
stream_options` as its parameter list, and a NIM attempt renders its
`extra_body.chat_template_kwargs`. No console errors. Full `pytest -q`: 15
failed, 7598 passed, 38 skipped -- the standing baseline, unchanged.
